## Notes

- Tank and Gun Characteristics Charts 4.47 (Commonwealth, jp2 137), 4.48 (Italian, jp2 138), 4.49 (German, jp2 172): the ratings of one TOE Strength Point of each weapon system (definitions in 3.3). Read twice, from the archive.org scan and from the community chart PDFs (Commonwealth Charts.pdf p. 27, Axis Charts.pdf pp. 29-30): 0 of 729 cells differ.
- Cells as printed: plain numbers as integers, parenthesised or marked values as strings (a parenthesised rating cannot be used while any unit in the hex has ammunition and an unparenthesised rating of that kind), dashes and blanks as null. Close Assault is printed as Off/Def in one column; it is split here. bar is the Breakdown Adjustment Rating (columns left L or right R, or 0).
- class is ours: tank, artillery, anti-tank or anti-air from the chart's section headings. The German chart prints no heading over its artillery rows (7.5cm IG18 to 21cm mrs18); they are artillery here.
- marks keeps the printed footnote signs. Commonwealth: * a US tank (only changes how many fit a tank battalion-equivalent); † the Scorpion, a mine-clearing tank on a Valentine chassis, counts as engineers for minefields and arrives with two tank battalions returning in October 1942; ‡ the SP guns (Bishop, Priest, Deacon). Italian: * the Semovente 75/18 SP gun; *** ParaArt is 81mm mortars with light anti-tank guns, the only Italian gun that can be air-dropped; **** the 'I' AA points have no transport of their own (CPA 0+) and move only with trucks assigned; the Tobruk coast-defence artillery groups never move. German: *** captured Russian guns; **** a Czech 47mm gun on a Pz I chassis; the 7.5cm light infantry gun and 2.8cm anti-tank gun may be air-transported or dropped.
- before: values that apply until the Game-Turn given. The Italian 75/27 and German 7.5cm guns have anti-armour 0 until the first OpStage of January 1942 (Game-Turn 63; the Italian footnote misprints the year 11942). Every German tank has BAR 1R until Game-Turn 31.
- printed: three German rows are misaligned on the chart, and both reads agree on where the cells sit (kept in printed as a JSON list, CPA to BAR). Our realignment by the neighbouring rows: Pz III E as vulnerability -, armour 3, Off/Def 4/4, fuel 3, BAR 0 (compare Pz III H); 7.62cm Pak(R) and Marder III lack a cell, so their values move one column right; the Pak(R)'s CPA is 15 like every towed gun on the three charts, the Marder's is unknown (null). The 5cm Pak 38's Off/Def is printed 1½1, read as 1/1. All four are questions for the printed copy (decision board, copy group).
- oa_names maps each weapon name used on the OA sheets (data/oa/*.json toe[].weapon) to a row id. The Commonwealth 'French 149mm (see It. Arty)' points to the Italian chart's row. The Italian OA 'Heavy AA' is read as the 75/46 (the 90/53 is a separate row no sheet names). The Italian 'vv' is not a weapon name (an id code where a weapon was expected) and has no row.
